title: Directed singular-value sparsifiers with nearly optimal support
summary: Emile Anand reduces the support of strong singular-value sparsifiers for unweighted directed graphs to O(n log n/ε²) arcs and gives a randomized nearly-linear-time construction in the real-arithmetic model.

results.title: Directed singular-value sparsifiers with O(n log n/ε²) arcs
results.summary: Strong directed singular-value approximation now needs only O(n log n/ε²) reweighted original arcs while preserving every in-degree and out-degree exactly.
results.aiUse: The author reports exploring an expander-based approach with GPT-6 Astra; Claude Opus 5.5 subsequently helped flesh out the writing of the lemmas and proofs.
results.body:
**Theorem and model.** Let $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ be the adjacency matrix of an unweighted directed graph, with $m$ arcs, and let $0<\varepsilon<1$. Write $D_L=\operatorname{diag}(A\mathbf1)$, $D_R=\operatorname{diag}(A^\top\mathbf1)$ and $P=D_L^{-1/2}AD_R^{-1/2}$ after removing zero-degree coordinates. Anand constructs a nonnegative reweighting $\widetilde A$, supported only on original arcs, with exactly the same row and column sums and at most $O(n\log(2n)/\varepsilon^2)$ nonzeros. Its normalized matrix $\widetilde P$ obeys the *strong singular-value* condition

$$|x^\top(\widetilde P-P)y|\le\varepsilon\sqrt{\|x\|_2^2-\|P^\top x\|_2^2}\sqrt{\|y\|_2^2-\|Py\|_2^2}$$

for all $x,y$, including directions in which the defect vanishes. A randomized algorithm achieves this with probability at least $1-\eta$ in $\widetilde O(m+n)$ **real-arithmetic** operations, where the suppressed factors depend polynomially on $\log n$, $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $\log(1/\eta)$. Rational output weights have polynomial bit length. For positive weighted inputs with maximum-to-minimum weight ratio $U$, an existential bound adds $O(n\log(2U))$ arcs.

**Previous bounds.** Strong SV approximation, introduced by Ahmadinejad, Peebles, Pyne, Sidford and Vadhan, is stronger than ordinary directed cut approximation: it controls bilinear errors relative to the left and right Schur-complement defects and behaves well under products of transition operators. Lau, Wang and Zhou previously established an $O(n\log^5 n/\varepsilon^2)$-arc bound. Anand removes four logarithmic factors and gives a nearly-linear randomized construction, whereas their algorithm was deterministic. The familiar undirected benchmark of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava is $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$ edges; Anand also proves an $\Omega(\min\{n^2,n/\varepsilon^2\})$ directed lower bound, leaving only one logarithm in support size.

**Proof mechanism.** The directed matrix is lifted to a weighted bipartite graph, allowing effective-resistance decompositions to control the left and right defect metrics. The central projected-variance lemma analyzes perturbations after enforcing *both* degree constraints: each resistance piece contributes its own Schur-complement defect, without paying again for vertices shared by different pieces. This produces matrix-discrepancy estimates suitable for a partial coloring that drives a constant fraction of arc weights toward zero while preserving the margins.

The construction proceeds through repeated sparsification phases. In relatively sparse phases it uses constrained spectral projection; in dense phases, expander pruning produces cores with controlled covariance. Gaussian matrix bounds and a rotation argument show that projecting a Gaussian vector onto the degree-constrained cube yields low spectral discrepancy. Sparse Jacobi iterations implement the projection to sufficient precision. Cycle rounding then deletes arcs while preserving every in-degree and out-degree exactly. A stability lemma composes the phasewise errors despite changes in the defect metrics, and grid rounding bounds the bit length of the final weights.

**Significance and limits.** The result improves sparse representations of directed random walks, directed cuts and associated linear-algebraic primitives. Removing the remaining $\log n$ factor, obtaining an equally efficient weighted construction, derandomizing, and proving a word-RAM running time remain open. In particular, the stated nearly-linear complexity must **not** be interpreted as a bit-complexity guarantee.

**AI use and verification.** The paper's AI disclosure says the author explored an expander-based approach with GPT-6 Astra and that Claude Opus 5.5 helped develop the written lemmas and proofs. This is an arXiv v1 preprint, announced November 11, 2026; no proof-assistant formalization or completed peer review is stated. The account is based on the complete arXiv HTML manuscript, not merely its abstract.
